extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians serving as reviewers for the zbMATH Prague Editorial Unit (registered zbMATH reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing, formatting, submitting, and managing reviews of mathematical works for the zbMATH Prague Editorial Unit, including content, style, legal and organizational requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and scope of the review
rubrics_metrics.description: A review of a mathematical work should give a brief and clear account of its contents. Reading the review is not intended to be a substitute for reading the original paper; the primary purpose is to help the user to decide whether he or she needs to read the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Main results of the paper should be briefly described, preferably in a non-technical manner. For papers in applied mathematics, concentrate on the mathematical aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility for correctness and novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: You as a reviewer have, in principle, no responsibility for checking the correctness or novelty of the original, but if you do discover that it contains a significant error or that it overlaps significantly with other work, you should mention that fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention significant errors or substantial overlap with other work when discovered; otherwise detailed verification of correctness/novelty is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of authors' text and quoting
rubrics_metrics.description: If you come to the conclusion that the summary or another part of the paper’s text describes the contents in the best way, you may decide to take such a text as (part of) your review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using extensive direct quotes from the original, clearly label them as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should preferably be written in English; reviews in French or German will also be accepted. They should be clear in style and consistent with the standards of usage in the language chosen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reader with a moderate knowledge of the language in question should be able to understand the review. In case of a translated title of the original, please check its correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended length and focus
rubrics_metrics.description: The review may vary in length from a few lines to a more elaborate text, depending particularly on your evaluation of the importance of the work you review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust length to the importance of the work: short for minor items, longer for substantial contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: File format and TeX usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Please prepare your review in TeX without using self-defined Macros (LaTeX is preferred but all TeX styles are supported).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use user-defined macros. Use LaTeX where possible to ensure consistent processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of nonessential elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Please do not include tables, large diagrams, drawings or formulas of minor importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include only essential formulas/figures; avoid large nonessential graphics that complicate typesetting or reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Font and emphasis usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Please use alternative fonts (bold, italics etc.) only if necessary, e.g. in formulas or for highlighting the authors of cited publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve font changes for necessary emphasis; follow examples given for citation formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: References to related work
rubrics_metrics.description: References to related work are always appreciated. When giving references, please try to be as specific and accurate as possible so that the references can be identified unambiguously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the provided reference patterns (examples given for journal article and book including Zbl codes). Try to find the corresponding entry in zbMATH and indicate correct metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference formatting examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the example patterns provided for journal articles and books (including Zbl identifiers and punctuation/italics) when giving references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example 1: journal article (Zbl 1170.35066) [{\it J. Krieger} et al., Duke Math. J. 147, No. 1, 1--53 (2009; Zbl 1170.35066)]. Example 2: book (Zbl 1151.55001) [{\it J. Barge} and {\it J. Lannes}, Suites de Sturm, indice de Maslov et p\'eriodicit\'e de Bott. Basel: Birkh\"auser (2008; Zbl 1151.55001)].

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor is proofreading the submitted reviews. However, given the amount of processed entries we cannot send you proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is thus extremely important that the content of your manuscript is as accurate as possible before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject classification (MSC 2010)
rubrics_metrics.description: The publications you receive for reviewing are usually classified by the authors or our editors according to the Mathematics Subject Classification (MSC) 2010.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the suggested MSC codes and complete or correct them if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keywords
rubrics_metrics.description: Please describe the publication’s content with a set of keywords that give a quick outline of the subjects covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there are preassigned keywords, you may also use (some of) them if you consider them suitable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacting the editorial office
rubrics_metrics.description: Inform the editor as early and precisely as possible about any changes of your address, e-mail address or fields of interest so that we can correct our files and keep in contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also notify the office if you wish to receive fewer or more articles/books, or wish a hiatus. If you do not want to review a particular paper, return it as soon as possible with a short comment and perhaps recommend another reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery methods for review material
rubrics_metrics.description: Books to be reviewed will be sent to you via normal mail. Articles will be provided in PDF format by a download link in the inviting e-mail message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of the delivery channel and handle materials accordingly (e.g., delete per publisher rules when required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: If possible, please provide us with your review within eight weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need more time for your review, please let us know as soon as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review submission channel
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be delivered electronically via our web interface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In case of any problems please contact the editor. Reviews requested by the Prague Editorial Unit should be submitted exclusively via our web interface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of reviews for international editorial units
rubrics_metrics.description: You may sometimes receive material for reviewing from cooperating external editorial units in different countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When material comes from external units, be sure to send your review back to the respective cooperating unit (not necessarily to Prague), unless the request is explicitly from the Prague unit (in which case submit via Prague web interface).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer transfers onto FIZ Karlsruhe all exclusive exploitation rights relating to the reviews of zbMATH in printed or electronical form as well as the right for adaptation of the delivered reviews, these rights worldwide and for an indefinite period of time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The zbMATH editorial office of FIZ Karlsruhe is entitled to assigning these rights to third persons or to grant non-exclusive rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storage and use of personal data
rubrics_metrics.description: We notify that we store your address and your fields of interest electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These data are used exclusively by the editorial office in connection with your task as a reviewer for zbMATH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on use of electronic review copies
rubrics_metrics.description: E-books and articles that we make available to you electronically may only be used for reviewing purposes; in particular, legal regulations prohibit the circulation of these documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depending on the publishers’ terms and conditions, the review copy may have to be deleted after submitting the review. For detailed information please see the cover page of the respective article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer benefits and compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Hardcopies of books and articles that you have reviewed remain your property. In compensation for your out-of-pocket expenses, you will be credited with a flat rate of 3.00 euros per review (excluding book reviews and authors' abstracts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You will find an overview of your credit within your Reviewer Account. The credit can be used for book orders (with a 20% EMS Publishing House discount), donated, or paid out. Place book orders within your zbMATH Open Reviewer Account.
